digest.component_or_area: LLM provider seam and runtime abstraction
propositions: rebar's LLM runtime is architecturally Anthropic-shaped with hardcoded provider-name branches and refusals that prevent Bedrock and OpenAI-compatible endpoint support despite documented env vars and capability gaps vs pydantic-ai's extension points.

AWS Bedrock-hosted Claude is a first-class use case for rebar's clients but has no native integration path; the proposed OpenAI-compatible gateway workaround silently loses prompt caching, retrying transport, read timeouts, and structured output.

Capability flags and output-mode selection are hardcoded against provider name strings rather than reading pydantic-ai's ModelProfile, preventing Bedrock (which has different cache and capability semantics than direct Anthropic) from declaring its actual capabilities.

The signed verdict sidecar records a model string that no longer names the actual provider or endpoint when routed through a gateway, losing provenance transparency needed to distinguish first-class verdicts from best-effort ones.
REBAR_LLM_BASE_URL and REBAR_LLM_API_KEY are documented as working but actively refused by _pai_check_config, making the documentation false.

A provider-factory seam accepting pydantic-ai's ModelProfile override, two-tier support (first-class Anthropic+Bedrock, best-effort OpenAI-compatible), and structured provenance in the verdict sidecar are achievable with pydantic-ai 1.107.1's existing extension points without inventing rebar-specific hooks.
